comparison: Perfect agreement on NBD conformational changes (C28-C35). Both evaluations find the PELDOR data convincing and well-supported, with reviewers explicitly affirming 'convincing biophysical support for the dynamic behavior' and OpenEval noting the data 'clearly demonstrate nucleotide-dependent conformational changes.'

Perfect agreement on lateral gate-1 findings (C36-C42). Both evaluations support the claims, with reviewers describing experiments as 'well-designed and well-executed' and OpenEval confirming the data 'clearly show nucleotide-dependent conformational changes at lateral gate-1.'

Strong agreement on lateral gate-2 heterogeneity and LptC modulation (C43-C54). OpenEval addresses C43-C54 while peer review covers C43-C57 (including speculative claims C55-C56). Both find the data well-supported, with reviewers highlighting this as a 'notable new insight' and OpenEval noting the data are 'well-documented.'

Partial overlap on β-jellyroll domain findings. OpenEval focuses on stable LptF-LptG interactions (C5, C58-C59, C95), while peer review addresses broader β-jellyroll dynamics (C58-C65) including both LptF and LptG domains. Both evaluations are supportive of the data quality.

Partial overlap on LptF β-jellyroll allosteric coupling. OpenEval addresses C6, C60-C62, C96, C99 focusing on ATP-dependent changes in LptF, while peer review covers C58-C65 addressing both LptF and LptG domains more broadly. Both find the allosteric coupling findings significant and well-supported.

Partial overlap on LptG β-jellyroll behavior. OpenEval addresses C64-C65, C103 showing nucleotide-independent behavior, while peer review covers broader β-jellyroll findings (C58-C65). Both evaluations support the differential regulation between LptF and LptG domains.

Minimal overlap on LptF-LptC interactions. OpenEval addresses stable β-jellyroll interactions (C66, C107), while peer review focuses on TM-LptC dynamics and insertion/removal (C66-C78). Both are supportive, but address different aspects of LptC behavior.

Strong agreement on LptC modulation of lateral gate-2. OpenEval addresses C9, C71-C78 focusing on the reduction of heterogeneity upon LptC binding, while peer review covers C66-C78 including broader TM-LptC dynamics. Both highlight this as a key mechanistic insight regarding TM-LptC insertion and release.

Agreement on TM-LptC dissociation in vanadate-trapped state (C67-C70). OpenEval finds the data supportive with appropriate caveats about incomplete trapping, while peer review emphasizes this as addressing a key knowledge gap about 'insertion and removal of the TM helix of LptC.'

Perfect agreement on LILBID-MS findings (C79-C82). Both evaluations support the LPS binding and release data, with reviewers noting the approach 'provides insight into the order of operations' and OpenEval confirming the mass spectrometry 'clearly shows LPS-bound complexes' and release patterns.

Perfect agreement on TM-LptC dynamic behavior (C114-C117). Both evaluations support the integration of PELDOR and LILBID-MS data showing dynamic TM-LptC behavior, with reviewers highlighting insights into 'spatial organization of the LptC domain' and OpenEval noting consistency with structural observations.

Partial overlap on coordinated conformational changes. OpenEval addresses C7, C85-C86 focusing on NBD and lateral gate coordination, while peer review covers C85-C86, C88-C90, C94 including membrane environment effects. Both support the validation of structural observations in solution.

Strong agreement on membrane environment effects (C88-C90, C93-C94). Both evaluations support the proteoliposome findings, with reviewers emphasizing this as 'crucial' for providing 'valuable dynamics information in the lipid environment' and OpenEval noting the broader distributions are 'clearly demonstrated.'

Perfect agreement on variant functionality validation (C122-C124). Both evaluations accept that spin-labeled variants retain function, with reviewers describing experiments as 'well-designed and well-executed' and OpenEval noting the validation through ATPase activity and expected conformational changes.

Strong agreement on background knowledge (C1-C4, C10-C19). OpenEval addresses established background about Lpt system and LPS biology, while peer review covers broader background (C1-C27) including structural context. Both treat this as accepted foundational knowledge without challenge.

Partial overlap on prior structural work. OpenEval addresses C20-C26, C83-C84 summarizing structural studies, while peer review covers C1-C27 including this structural context. Both accept this as accurate background establishing the study's motivation.

Minimal overlap on speculative functional interpretations. OpenEval rates C27, C55-C56, C63, C87, C98, C102, C105-C106, C108, C110-C111 as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct validation, while peer review addresses C55-C56 within broader lateral gate-2 findings (C43-C57) and rates them SUPPORTED. Divergence reflects different treatment of speculative mechanistic claims.

Minimal overlap on β-jellyroll functional speculation. OpenEval includes C63 among UNCERTAIN speculative claims about functional roles, while peer review addresses it within broader β-jellyroll findings (C58-C65) rated SUPPORTED. Reflects different thresholds for accepting functional interpretations.

Minimal overlap on mechanistic model. OpenEval includes C98 (contradicted proposal) among UNCERTAIN claims, while peer review addresses C99, C118-C120 as SUPPORTED mechanistic insights. Both address speculative aspects but with different claim groupings and evaluation outcomes.

Agreement on mechanistic model with different confidence levels. OpenEval rates C118-C120 as UNCERTAIN noting the model is 'plausible and consistent with the data, but lacks direct experimental validation,' while peer review rates C99, C118-C120 as SUPPORTED, treating the model as logical conclusion from data. Key divergence in evaluation of speculative mechanistic proposals.

OpenEval addresses prior functional studies (C97, C104, C113) establishing domain importance, rating them SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific background claims.

OpenEval addresses factual statements about experimental methods and protein classification (C91-C92, C121), rating them SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological details.
OpenEval addresses structural features of LptF (C100-C101) as SUPPORTED background. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific structural details.
OpenEval addresses poor resolution of β-jellyroll domains in structures (C109) as SUPPORTED observation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific structural limitation.
